message:
Resolver v3.0: descend with reads and write begins together

TempConflictBTree's checkReads descends once for a batch's reads and the
begins of its writes, and prepares the leaves the writes will reach.
addWrites applies the accepted writes from those prepared leaves.
checkReads is instantiated with 16 tasks.

fdbcompat.h's VectorRef gains empty(), BTreeV2.cpp is renamed BTreeV3.cpp,
and the TempConflictBTree tests are adapted to the new write path.

Resolver v3.1: apply each batch's writes through a write cursor, and integrate btree-v3 in FDB

A write cursor applies a batch's writes. It cleans a leaf once per batch
and cutoff, buffers only the slices that have writes, reuses the split
candidates prepared by checkReads and coalesces accepted overlapping
writes. The TempConflictBTree tests use the write cursor.

The FDB resolver uses btree-v3. Positions are assigned after sorting,
checkReads runs on every batch and accepted writes are applied from the
prepared leaves. BTREE_V3_TASKS sets the task capacity. BTreeV3.cpp,
ConflictSet, CMakeLists.txt, By5ResolverTest.inc, SmokeReplay.inc and
by5eval/by5-acct.py are updated for it.

The benchmarks are part of this version:
- blocksizebench measures btree-v1, v2 and v3 from one source;
- EvalBench.inc and MacBenchmark.inc measure the conflict set;
- each benchmark times its whole batch and every phase of it, including
  adding the transactions and sorting.
skiplisttest builds its conflict set after its data.

Resolver v3.2: keep prepared write destinations valid across leaf releases and splits

Prepared write destinations stay valid across leaf releases and splits,
without a tree-wide epoch or searches from the root while writes are
applied. LeafBlockLayout gains firstWrite, the representative of the
write groups prepared for a leaf. The tests apply a single write as a
one-transaction batch through checkReads and addWrites.

Resolver v3.3: check a write destination's right neighbour only when needed

A write destination's right neighbour is checked only after a split, a
redirection or an ambiguous expired boundary.

Resolver v3.5: union accepted writes in one streamed pass and prefetch destination leaves

Each batch's accepted writes are united by endpoint index in one streamed
pass. Whole destination leaves are prefetched a few groups ahead. PagePool
selects base, THP or HugeTLB backing.

Resolver v3.6: apply accepted writes through two alternating groups of staged leaf tasks

Accepted writes are applied through two alternating groups of staged leaf
tasks that prefetch leaves and search keys stage by stage. A task reuses
the in-leaf position across its writes. The write lookahead defaults to
8 groups.

Resolver v3.7: advance each write task to its next prefetch in one visit

Each write task advances to its next prefetch in one visit. Blocked tasks
are parked out of dispatch until they reach the head. A cached destination
representative is reused while it stays a root.

Resolver v3.8: prepare each write interval once and add a three-group policy

Each write interval is prepared once. Short keys are hinted without a
loop, known local steps are chained, the parent prefetch is dropped and
advance stays out of line. RESOLVER1_WRITE_GROUPS adds a three-group
write policy; the default stays two groups.

Resolver v3.9 (experiment): split write-search continuations into fast and slow paths

Write-search continuations run through a small inlined fast path.
Reservation, ownership, cleanup and mutations stay in an out-of-line slow
path.

Resolver v3.10 (experiment): replace the fixed write groups with a runnable ring

The fixed write groups are replaced with a runnable ring, refilled to
twice the service quantum at each turn.

Resolver v3.11 (experiment): interleave grouped writes on distinct leaves

Grouped writes on distinct leaves run interleaved with independent owners.
Unproven groups are kept as exclusive barriers.

Resolver v3.12 (experiment): keep two free slots in each concurrently written leaf

Each concurrently written leaf keeps two free slots, so local writers never
create a pending split in a shared ancestor.

Resolver v3.13 (experiment): schedule independent leaf components cooperatively

Independent leaf components are scheduled cooperatively. Groups that share
leaves are absorbed, without a writer head or exclusive barriers.

Resolver v3.14 (experiment): prepare write footprints with interleaved walkers

Write footprints are prepared with interleaved walkers that prefetch each
leaf and key before reading it.

Resolver v3.15 (experiment): schedule writer tasks in per-state bitmaps

Writer tasks are scheduled in per-state bitmaps. Each visit enters
directly at its state, without a per-task step switch.

Resolver v3.16 (experiment): serve PrepareInput and KeyMore first in each round

PrepareInput and KeyMore are served first in each round, so their
prefetches precede CompareSearch and InspectRight.

Resolver v3.17 (experiment): retire covered interior leaves whole during the write scan

Covered interior leaves are retired whole during the write scan, each one
checked against its last live entry. Tests cover the retirement.
